name: Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava Connecting to the Roof of Left-Sided Atrium
aliases: Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava with Left Atrial Drainage

criteria.description: Visualization of persistent left superior vena cava draining into the roof of the left atrium by echocardiography, CT angiography, or MRI
Absence or hypoplasia of right superior vena cava or anomalous venous return patterns
Evidence of right-to-left shunting such as unexplained hypoxemia or paradoxical embolism

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of persistent left superior vena cava draining into the left atrium
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies primarily on advanced cardiovascular imaging modalities; genetic testing is not typically contributory.

pathognomonic.notes: Central cyanosis often present in neonates or infants
searchTerms: blue skin from blood shunting right to left
cyanosis caused by abnormal blood flow
low oxygen causing bluish skin color

pathognomonic.notes: Stroke or systemic embolism from venous thrombi bypassing pulmonary circulation

common.notes: Low oxygen saturation without primary pulmonary disease
searchTerms: low blood oxygen detected by pulse oximeter
oxygen deficiency shown on pulse monitor

common.notes: Often due to associated cardiac anomalies

occasional.notes: Arrhythmias may occur due to atrial dilation
Due to pulmonary hypoperfusion or associated anomalies
In severe cases with significant shunting

rare.notes: Due to paradoxical embolism of septic emboli

searchTerms: weakness on one side after stroke

rare.notes: Secondary to chronic hypoxemia or associated defects

laboratory: Normal routine blood counts unless complications
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating persistent left superior vena cava draining into left atrium
CT angiography or cardiac MRI confirming anomalous venous return
Bubble contrast echocardiography showing right-to-left shunt
other: Electrocardiogram may show atrial enlargement or arrhythmias
Pulse oximetry revealing decreased oxygen saturation

distinguishingFeatures: Pulmonary veins drain anomalously rather than superior vena cava
Drainage into coronary sinus rather than left atrium

redFlags: Sudden onset neurological deficits indicating paradoxical embolism
Severe unexplained hypoxemia in neonate or infant
Recurrent strokes or systemic emboli without cardiac arrhythmia
references: Goyal SK, Punnam SR, Verma G, Ruberg FL. Persistent left superior vena cava: a case report and review of literature. Cardiovasc Ultrasound. 2008;6:50.
Buirski G, De Souza A. Persistent left superior vena cava with drainage into the left atrium: clinical and echocardiographic features. Am Heart J. 1982;103(5):927-931.
Orphanet: Persistent left superior vena cava connecting to the roof of left-sided atrium. ORPHA:99111.
